motion.name: flap
motion.value: 360ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); rotateX(90deg) -> rotateX(-8deg) at 60% -> 0, brightness(1.6) -> none
motion.purpose: A changed character flipping in on re-render.

motion.name: flap-stagger
motion.purpose: Left-to-right stagger across a flap word; only changed characters flip.

motion.name: idle
motion.purpose: Blank flap cells pulsing while the forecast loads.

components.name: Flap Word
components.description: Changing values set one character per translucent split-flap cell; the current temperature at display size.
components.html: 20°
components.css: .ds-ground { padding: 14px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #2675bb, #1f6fb4); } .ds-flaps { display: inline-flex; gap: 2px; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-size: 66px; font-weight: 700; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #ffffff; perspective: 300px; } .ds-f { position: relative; display: inline-block; min-width: 46px; padding: 2px 2px 0; text-align: center; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.16); border-radius: 2px; line-height: 1; } .ds-f.ds-deg { min-width: 30px; } .ds-f::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 50%; height: 1px; background: rgba(6,40,82,0.35); } .ds-flip { animation: ds-flap 360ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) both; } @keyframes ds-flap { 0% { transform: rotateX(90deg); filter: brightness(1.6); } 60% { transform: rotateX(-8deg); } 100% { transform: rotateX(0); filter: none; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-flip { animation: none; } }

components.name: Lead Plate
components.description: The full-width sun plate: the next change, and when. No split hairline at this size.
components.css: .ds-ground { padding: 14px; background: #1f6fb4; } .ds-lead { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; height: 38px; margin: 0; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #ffd166; color: #3b2a0a; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-size: 19px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-lf { display: inline-flex; gap: 1px; } .ds-lf > span { display: inline-block; min-width: 0.66em; padding: 0 1px; text-align: center; background: #f4c04f; border-radius: 2px; line-height: 1.3; }

narrative.overview:
Hawa reads the day's weather the way a station board reads departures: what changes next, and when. The board is set against the sky of the place it reports on. By day the ground is a classic sky blue, brighter at the top where the big temperature sits and deeper under the rows. By night (when the location's `is_day` is 0) it turns deep navy. On that ground sit translucent split-flap cells, hairline-seamed rows, and white condensed caps with tabular figures. Rank comes from size, weight, case and a few small warm plates, never from cards.

Density is high and calm. Everything sits on one 14px gutter inside a 360px column, and rows are uniform 34px timetable lines. The text itself is all near-white, so hierarchy comes from weight and size rather than from dimming. Warmth (sun yellow and peach) appears only as plates with dark warm ink: the brand chip, the lead row, the NOW chip, and the primary button. Meteocons, the product's bundled icon set, sit in the SKY column at row size.

Motion belongs to the flaps. When fresh data lands, only the characters that changed flip in, one after another from left to right. When nothing changed, the board stays still.
keyCharacteristics: A sky-blue ground by day and a navy ground by night, following the location's own daylight
Translucent white flap cells split by a navy hairline; white caps with tabular figures
Warm colour only as plates with dark warm ink; never as text on the sky
Hairline seams between rows; no cards, no shadows; the ground is the only gradient
Rain at 30% or more is a white chip with blue ink
Only changed characters flip, staggered left to right; still under reduced motion

rules.name: The Warm Plate Rule
rules.body: Warm colours appear only as plate fills carrying warm ink: brand chip, lead row, NOW chip, primary button. The single exception is the WEEK underline in peach. Never set warm-coloured text on the sky.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: The rain chip appears only at a 30% chance or more, and alert blush appears only on an app error. A dry hour and a working app show neither.

rules.name: The Readable Sky Rule
rules.body: Text must reach 4.5:1 against the sky at its own position (3:1 for text at 24px, or 18.66px bold, and up), measured on the brightest stop it can sit on. The top of the day gradient is the bright end. Darken the ground or use a well there; never accept a lower ratio.

rules.name: The Caps Board Rule
rules.body: Everything on the board is set in caps: labels, values, rows and buttons. Only full sentences (notice text, hints, credits, city detail lines) stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Dimming Rule
rules.body: Every ink is near-white, so a secondary role steps down in weight (700 to 600 to 500) and size, never into a grey.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular everywhere (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the body). Numeric columns are right-aligned.

rules.name: The Local Casing Rule
rules.body: Place names take `lang="tr"` or `lang="az"` only when the name contains a Turkish- or Azeri-specific letter. That way CSS uppercasing maps i to İ correctly, and English exonyms such as "Izmir" stay IZMIR.

rules.name: The Sky Ground Rule
rules.body: The only gradient is the page ground: a vertical sky, by day or by night. Components are flat translucent fills or opaque plates, with no shadows, glows or gradients of their own.

dos: **Do** set the ground from the location's own daylight: the day sky while the sun is up there, the night navy after.
**Do** set changing values (temperature, lead text) as flap cells, and flip only the characters that changed, staggered 45ms from left to right.
**Do** turn every flip and idle pulse off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
**Do** put inputs, quiet buttons and segments in a well so their text holds contrast on the bright sky.
**Do** separate rows and regions with 1px seams, and keep rows at 34px on the 14px gutter.
**Do** step secondary text down by weight and size, since all inks are near-white.
**Do** use tabular figures and right-align numeric columns.
donts: **Don't** set yellow or peach as text on the sky; warm colour is a plate with warm ink.
**Don't** group content in cards, panels or rounded containers; cells hold characters and controls, never sections.
**Don't** add box shadows or glows, or give a component its own gradient.
**Don't** show the rain chip below a 30% chance, or alert blush outside an app error.
**Don't** draw the split hairline across characters at lead-row size on a plate; at that size it reads as a strikethrough.
**Don't** replace the Meteocons with another icon set or with glyph characters.
**Don't** flip characters that did not change, and don't animate on first paint.
